{"id": "f3903c98-4adc-4a06-aa32-0dfe84c48f77", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "We're about to merge PR #14 in acme/payments-infra. It's the first infrastructure PR in that repo, there's no pipeline review set up, and finance wants to know what this stack is going to add to the AWS bill every month before we approve it. Can you work that out from the PR?

The attached material is what the repository integration and the AWS tools returned for this change. It is a synthetic test fixture: resource names, account results, SKUs and rates are made up, and the rates intentionally differ from real AWS list prices, so treat the rows below as the live lookup results for this run.

--- PR #14 (feature/ledger -> main) ---
Base branch main: no cloudformation/ directory.
Files added: cloudformation/payments-ledger.yaml, .github/workflows/deploy.yml

--- .github/workflows/deploy.yml (excerpt) ---
env:
  AWS_REGION: eu-west-1
  STACK_NAME: payments-ledger
run: aws cloudformation deploy --stack-name payments-ledger --template-file cloudformation/payments-ledger.yaml --region eu-west-1

--- cloudformation/payments-ledger.yaml (Resources; Parameters hold only VPC and subnet IDs) ---
  LedgerDbSubnetGroup: {Type: AWS::RDS::DBSubnetGroup, Properties: {SubnetIds: [!Ref PrivateSubnetA, !Ref PrivateSubnetB]}}
  LedgerDb:
    Type: AWS::RDS::DBInstance
    Properties: {Engine: postgres, DBInstanceClass: db.r6g.large, MultiAZ: true, AllocatedStorage: "200", StorageType: gp3, DBSubnetGroupName: !Ref LedgerDbSubnetGroup}
  ReconcilerNatEip: {Type: AWS::EC2::EIP, Properties: {Domain: vpc}}
  ReconcilerNatGateway: {Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway, Properties: {AllocationId: !GetAtt ReconcilerNatEip.AllocationId, SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnetA}}
  AlbSecurityGroup: {Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup}
  ApiLoadBalancer:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer
    Properties: {Type: application, Scheme: internet-facing, Subnets: [!Ref PublicSubnetA, !Ref PublicSubnetB], SecurityGroups: [!Ref AlbSecurityGroup]}
  ArchiveBucket: {Type: AWS::S3::Bucket, Properties: {VersioningConfiguration: {Status: Enabled}}}
  ReconcilerRole: {Type: AWS::IAM::Role}
  ReconcilerFunction: {Type: AWS::Lambda::Function, Properties: {Runtime: python3.12, Architectures: [arm64], MemorySize: 512, Role: !GetAtt ReconcilerRole.Arn}}

--- AWS (read-only), eu-west-1 ---
cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name payments-ledger
  -> ValidationError: Stack with id payments-ledger does not exist

--- pricing get-products (endpoint us-east-1, filter regionCode=eu-west-1), OnDemand terms only ---
AmazonRDS  SKU FX-RDS-01  usagetype EU-Multi-AZUsage:db.r6g.large   databaseEngine=PostgreSQL deploymentOption=Multi-AZ   0.500 USD per Hrs
AmazonRDS  SKU FX-RDS-09  usagetype EU-UnusedBox:db.r6g.large       databaseEngine=PostgreSQL deploymentOption=Multi-AZ   0.000 USD per Hrs   "unused capacity reservation hour"
AmazonRDS  SKU FX-RDS-02  usagetype EU-RDS:Multi-AZ-GP3-Storage     volumeType=General Purpose-GP3 databaseEngine=PostgreSQL   0.250 USD per GB-Mo
AmazonEC2  SKU FX-NAT-01  usagetype EU-NatGateway-Hours             productFamily=NAT Gateway   0.050 USD per Hrs
AmazonEC2  SKU FX-NAT-02  usagetype EU-NatGateway-Bytes             productFamily=NAT Gateway   0.050 USD per GB
AmazonVPC  SKU FX-IP-01   usagetype EU-PublicIPv4:InUseAddress                                  0.005 USD per Hrs
AWSELB     SKU FX-ALB-01  usagetype EU-LoadBalancerUsage            productFamily=Load Balancer-Application   0.025 USD per Hrs
AWSELB     SKU FX-ALB-03  usagetype EU-TS-LoadBalancerUsage         productFamily=Load Balancer-Application   0.006 USD per Hrs   "trust store unit-hour"
AWSELB     SKU FX-ALB-02  usagetype EU-LCUUsage                     productFamily=Load Balancer-Application   0.008 USD per LCU-Hrs", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "8dad530d-c805-42ea-8136-67718014b830", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "thinking", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "This is a self-contained calculation with all pricing data already provided, so I can compute the monthly cost directly without delegating. I'll use 730 hours per month as the standard AWS assumption and start tallying costs starting with the RDS db.r6g.large Multi-AZ instance.

Adding up the storage comes to $415/mo for RDS. Then for the NAT gateway and EIP, I'm pulling hourly rates plus noting that data processing charges are usage-based and unknown, so I'll flag that as variable. I'm also noting the subtlety around public IPv4 charges applying to in-use addresses since February 2024, and considering whether the ALB's implicit IP factors into this the same way.

Moving to the ALB costs, I'm calculating hourly usage charges, checking whether the trust store fee applies (it doesn't since mutual TLS isn't configured, but I'll mention it as conditional), and now I'm pulling the LCU usage rate to factor into the total.

Then checking the ArchiveBucket - there's no S3 pricing SKU in the fixture, so I need to flag that as missing data rather than compute a cost. Similarly, ReconcilerFunction's Lambda pricing isn't in the fixture either, so that's also flagged as missing/usage-based, while the IAM role, security group, and subnet group are all free resources with no cost implications.

Adding up the fixed monthly costs - RDS instance, RDS storage, NAT gateway, EIP, and ALB hourly charges - gives me a subtotal of $473.40. Beyond that, I still need to flag several usage-dependent costs that can't be computed without traffic estimates: NAT Gateway data processing, ALB LCU usage, ALB trust store hours (likely zero since mTLS isn't configured), and S3 storage/request costs.

I'm noticing that S3 storage/requests for ArchiveBucket and Lambda invocation/duration for ReconcilerFunction both returned no pricing data at all, so I'll need to flag those as gaps requiring additional lookups. This is a straightforward computation from data already provided, so no need to delegate further - I can present the $473.40 fixed baseline plus caveats about variable and missing pricing directly. I'll use AWS's standard 730 hours/month convention and now work through the precise math for each line item.

RDS instance comes to $365.00, storage adds $50.00, NAT gateway hours are $36.50, EIP hours are $3.65, and ALB hours contribute $18.25 - summing to that $473.40 fixed floor. I'll present this breakdown clearly, noting the variable add-ons (NAT data processing, ALB LCU-hours) and the missing S3/Lambda pricing, and offer to pull those additional figures if needed.

"}]}

{"id": "a2d3ea38-25b3-4385-9293-a8448946ba6c", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Based on the PR, here's the monthly cost breakdown for the `payments-ledger` stack in `eu-west-1`, using the pricing lookups you pulled (730 hrs/month):

**Fixed/predictable costs**

| Resource | SKU | Rate | Monthly |
|---|---|---|---|
| RDS `db.r6g.large`, Multi-AZ, PostgreSQL | FX-RDS-01 | $0.500/hr | $365.00 |
| RDS gp3 storage, 200 GB | FX-RDS-02 | $0.250/GB-mo | $50.00 |
| NAT Gateway (hourly) | FX-NAT-01 | $0.050/hr | $36.50 |
| Elastic IP (attached to NAT GW) | FX-IP-01 | $0.005/hr | $3.65 |
| ALB (hourly) | FX-ALB-01 | $0.025/hr | $18.25 |
| **Subtotal** | | | **$473.40/mo** |

That's the floor — it runs even at zero traffic.

**Usage-based, can't be pinned down from the PR alone**
- **NAT Gateway data processing** (FX-NAT-02, $0.050/GB) — scales with reconciler egress traffic, no volume estimate available.
- **ALB LCU-hours** (FX-ALB-02, $0.008/LCU-Hr) — scales with connections/bandwidth/rule evaluations. Template doesn't configure a trust store, so the $0.006/hr trust-store SKU (FX-ALB-03) shouldn't apply.
- **S3 (`ArchiveBucket`)** — versioning is enabled, but no S3 storage/request SKU came back in this pricing pull, so I can't price it. Need a follow-up lookup.
- **Lambda (`ReconcilerFunction`)** — arm64, 512MB — same issue, no Lambda SKU returned, so invocation/duration cost is unestimated.

**Bottom line for finance:** expect a minimum of **~$473/month** just to keep this stack running idle, before any ledger traffic, reconciler data transfer, archive storage, or Lambda invocations are factored in. The real number will be higher once those variable pieces are added.

Want me to pull the missing S3 and Lambda pricing so we can close that gap, or estimate the NAT/ALB usage-based costs against an assumed traffic volume?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
